newsitem.title: CANADA: CBRS confirms Quebec ratings after budget.
newsitem.headline: CBRS confirms Quebec ratings after budget.

text.p: Canadian Bond Rating Agency on Wednesday said it reaffirmed the ratings of the Province of Quebec, Hydro-Quebec and entities guaranteed by the province at A with a negative outlook.
The ratings agency also reaffirmed the ratings of the province's treasury bills and the commercial paper of Hydro-Quebec and other guaranteed entities at A-1+ with a negative outlook.
The Province of Quebec yesterday released its budget for 1997/98 and forecast a deficit of C$2.2 billion. The province has said it plans to eliminate its deficit in 1999-2000.

CBRS said while it recognises that Quebec has reached its budgetary targets for 1997-1998, it maintained the negative rating out because of the continued deficit, high debt levels, and difficult economic conditions found in the province.

The agency also said it is concerned with the magnitude of the upcoming C$500 million transfer of responsibilities to the Quebec municipalities. CBRS said it will continue to review the impact on municipalities on a case by case basis.

CBRS said given the level of accumulated debt and debt service payments, it will take several years for Quebec to remedy its financial situation. The agency said in order to improve its credit rating outlook, Quebec will have to significantly reduce its debt levels.

The ratings agency also noted that since only part of the Quebec employee pension plan's obligations have been included in the Public Accounts computations, Quebec's auditor general has questioned the real level of Quebec's deficit. CBRS said the difference would increase the deficit by C$1 billion and the province will review the possibility of adjusting the accounting proceedures to include all of its obligations.
